title: Minimum Discards to Balance Inventory
summary: Given integers w and m, and an integer array arrivals where each element represents the type of item arriving on a specific day (days are 1-indexed), you must ensure that no item type appears more than m times in any w-day window by discarding the minimum number of arrivals.
statement: Given integers w and m, and an integer array arrivals where each element represents the type of item arriving on a specific day (days are 1-indexed), you must ensure that no item type appears more than m times in any w-day window by discarding the minimum number of arrivals. For each day i, the window is defined as the range from max(1, i - w + 1) to i. If keeping the arrival on day i would cause an item type to appear more than m times in this window, the arrival must be discarded.
constraints: Up to 100,000 arrivals, with one <= m <= w <= n.
Every kept type occurs at most m times in every trailing w-day window.
Discard only on arrival day and minimize discards.
reference_solution:
def minimum_inventory_discards(arrivals,w,m):
    counts={};kept=[False]*len(arrivals);answer=0
    for day,item in enumerate(arrivals):
        expired=day-w
        if expired>=0 and kept[expired]:counts[arrivals[expired]]-=1
        if counts.get(item,0)>=m:answer+=1
        else:kept[day]=True;counts[item]=counts.get(item,0)+1
    return answer

hints: For a fixed type, keeping an arrival whenever the current window has room cannot hurt future choices.
Track counts of kept arrivals only and expire the kept decision from exactly w days ago.
Discard when the type count is already m; otherwise mark the arrival kept and increment it.
An earlier kept item expires no later than a current one, so exchanging any optimal discard for the greedy keep never reduces future capacity.
